sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Assembly of Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) Battery Packs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 20–23, 31–35, 62, 214 and 233; Law 18/2022 amended the minimum capital rule for limited liability companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) for the province in which the registered office is located, under the Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Relations with the Courts.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), filed for registration in the competent Provincial Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 1. Contributions must be fully subscribed and paid when the company is formed; no general statutory escrow account is required. If capital is below EUR 3,000, the company must allocate at least 20% of annual profits to legal reserve until capital and reserve together reach EUR 3,000, and shareholders may have subsidiary liability for the shortfall on liquidation. Registry and notarial charges are tariff-based; the amount is not a single fixed national filing fee, and the USD figure above is not an estimate of total formation costs.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscriptions and contributions recorded in the deed of incorporation and acknowledge that the subscribed shares have been paid in accordance with applicable law. RESOLVED, that the registered office stated in the deed and articles of association be adopted as the Company’s registered office. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed [sole director/joint directors/board member] and [name] be appointed [managing director, if applicable], subject to acceptance and registration where required. RESOLVED, that the appointed officers be authorized to obtain the Company’s tax identification number, complete registry and beneficial-ownership filings, open bank accounts, and submit required industrial, environmental, municipal, and workplace applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Clear and reserve the company name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), using its official company-name certification service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request a negative name certificate for the proposed Spanish company name and alternatives. The certificate must be current when the notarial deed is executed and must identify the intended founder or applicant as required by the Registry.
required_dossiers: Proposed company names in order of preference
Applicant identification and authorization, if submitted by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is unavailable or confusingly similar to a registered name, submit alternative names and obtain a new certificate before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain founder identification and tax credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT); Spanish consulate or competent Spanish police office for identification formalities, as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Spanish tax identification number for each foreign founder or director who requires one. A non-resident individual generally requires an NIE; a foreign corporate founder requires a Spanish NIF and evidence of existence, authority, and beneficial ownership. Have foreign public documents apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish by a sworn translator where required.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity document
NIE or NIF applications and supporting documents
Foreign corporate registry extract and constitutional documents, if applicable
Board or shareholder authorization and representative power of attorney, if applicable
Beneficial-owner identification and ownership chart
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to AEAT or identification-office requests with corrected forms and certified evidence. Obtain apostilles, legalization, or sworn translations where requested; use a properly empowered Spanish representative if the applicant cannot attend.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the incorporation deed and pay in capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario) selected by the founders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the name certificate, articles of association, founder and director identification, capital and share-allocation details, registered-office address, and evidence of contributions. Execute the public deed. For cash contributions, provide bank evidence or use the statutory alternative under Companies Act Article 62(2), where the founders assume the prescribed responsibility for the reality of contributions. Non-cash contributions must be accurately described and valued.
required_dossiers: Current negative name certificate
Draft articles of association
Founder and director NIE/NIF and identification
Registered-office evidence
Bank certificate for cash contributions or applicable Article 62(2) declaration
Valuation and description of non-cash contributions, if any
Foreign documents, powers of attorney, apostilles or legalization, and sworn translations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct drafting, identity, contribution, or authority defects in a supplemental or rectifying notarial instrument. Replace an expired name certificate and provide any missing legalized or translated documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional tax identification and register for tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT, through the applicable electronic tax-registration service or competent tax office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Company’s provisional NIF and file the applicable census declaration, ordinarily Form 036, identifying the registered office, activity, tax obligations, and commencement information. The company must obtain its definitive NIF after registration and provide the registered deed and Commercial Registry evidence.
required_dossiers: Notarial incorporation deed
Founder or authorized representative identification
Provisional NIF application and Form 036
Registered-office and activity information
Commercial Registry registration evidence for definitive NIF
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct or supplement Form 036 and supporting evidence. Apply for or update the definitive NIF promptly after Commercial Registry registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the deed with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) for the province of the registered office; electronic filing may be made by the notary or an authorized representative.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed and required tax evidence for registration, ordinarily within two months of execution. Confirm the company’s registration particulars, directors, registered office, and articles against the filed deed. Obtain the registration certificate or extract and complete beneficial-ownership filings through the legally applicable channels.
required_dossiers: Authorized copy or electronically transmitted notarial deed
Current name certificate
Tax filing or exemption evidence required for registration
Director acceptance and identification details
Registered-office particulars
Beneficial-ownership information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address the Registrar’s written defect notice within its stated validity period by correcting the deed, supplying missing evidence, or executing a rectifying instrument. Seek review or appeal through the available Registry procedures if a defect is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the industrial establishment and secure site-level approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial authority of the Autonomous Community where the facility is located, through that region’s industrial-establishment registry and electronic portal; the relevant municipal authority handles planning, building, and activity approvals.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before construction, installation, or operation, confirm land-use compatibility and obtain required building and activity approvals from the municipality. Have the industrial installation designed and certified by qualified professionals, comply with applicable technical safety regulations, and file the establishment and relevant installations through the Autonomous Community’s industrial portal. Confirm whether the project requires an integrated environmental authorization, environmental impact assessment, or other environmental instrument before works commence.
required_dossiers: Company NIF and Commercial Registry evidence
Site title or lease and land-use compatibility evidence
Facility and process plans, capacity, and equipment schedule
Responsible technical project and installation certificates
Environmental screening or authorization documents, as applicable
Fire-safety and occupational-risk documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve technical or planning deficiencies identified by the regional or municipal authority; revise project documents, obtain additional studies, or apply for the required environmental instrument. Do not commence regulated operations until mandatory approvals and registrations are effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The industrial authority of the Autonomous Community in which the manufacturing facility is located; there is no single national industrial-licensing board. Municipal authorities separately control land use, building permits, and local activity or opening approvals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No single nationwide manufacturing permit title applies to every battery-pack assembly plant. The project generally requires the applicable municipal activity or environmental authorization and registration of the industrial establishment and regulated installations in the Autonomous Community’s industrial register. Exact instruments depend on location, process, capacity, and emissions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community, applying Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment; the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge is competent for projects reserved to the State.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific screening required. A LiFePO4 battery-pack assembly facility is not automatically subject to a full EIA solely because of its product. Full or simplified assessment may apply if the project falls within Annexes I or II of Law 21/2013, including by process, scale, location, or associated installations. Integrated environmental authorization under Legislative Royal Decree 1/2016 is required only if the installation falls within its listed industrial activities and thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single facility-wide numerical limit can be assigned without the site, process, and permit. Comply with the applicable integrated authorization or environmental permit, regional and municipal discharge conditions, the receiving sewer or water authority’s limits, air-emission requirements, and hazardous-waste rules. Characterize process effluent and emissions; segregate and manage electrolyte, contaminated materials, damaged cells, and other hazardous waste through authorized operators. Battery-specific obligations under Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 and applicable Spanish waste law must also be assessed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal building and activity approvals and comply with the industrial fire-safety regulation applicable on the filing and construction dates, including Royal Decree 164/2025 and its transitional provisions where applicable. Provide required fire-protection design, commissioning certificates, emergency planning, and inspections; obtain any required fire-service or municipal clearance. Structural safety and floor-loading must be demonstrated by competent technical professionals for the installed equipment and stored batteries. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, required risk assessments, worker training, emergency measures, and applicable workplace-installation regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); main electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la Agencia Tributaria (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es). For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the AEAT central registry is the relevant competent authority for national tax registration, corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident founder incorporating a Spanish SL must first obtain a provisional NIF for the company through the Mercantile Registry incorporation process or directly via AEAT Form 036/037 once the public deed is granted. The provisional NIF is converted into the definitive NIF after the SL is registered in the Mercantile Registry. Foreign entities without a Spanish branch that need a Spanish tax reference for VAT or withholding purposes must file Form 036 through a Spanish tax representative to obtain a non-resident NIF (NIF type N). The SL must also file the declaración censal (Form 036/037) before commencing any taxable activity, indicating the ISIC 2720 manufacturing activity, place of business, fiscal representative where relevant, and applicable indirect tax registrations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; a Spanish SL is always a separate taxable person for corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades). Available statutory elections include the optional group taxation regime for corporate income tax under Articles 58 et seq. of the Corporate Income Tax Law, the VAT group registration regime under Article 166 of the VAT Law, and the Spanish patent-box regime and participation exemption election where applicable. Hybrid mismatch rules transposing the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive (Law 11/2021) apply and are mandatory, not elective, but advance valuation agreements and advance pricing agreements are available with AEAT to reduce uncertainty on cross-border transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA) – Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold for a Spanish SL: any person or entity performing taxable business activities in Spain must be VAT-registered before commencing operations. For non-resident sellers using the EU One Stop Shop or Union OSS, a cross-border distance-sales threshold of EUR 10,000 per calendar year, measured on total cross-border distance sales into all EU Member States, applies above which Spanish VAT registration or OSS registration is mandatory. Reduced rates apply only to specifically listed goods and services; battery energy storage manufacturing is subject to the 21% standard rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain has phased-in mandatory business-to-business electronic invoicing under the Ley Crea y Crece framework; relevant documentation must be issued, transmitted, and stored in a structured electronic format. Large taxpayers with VAT turnover exceeding EUR 6 million are subject to the Immediate Supply of Information (SII) system, requiring electronic transmission of VAT books and invoice records to AEAT generally within eight calendar days. All invoice issuance software used by Spanish businesses must comply with VeriFactu technical standards, including QR generation and tamper-evident encryption. Spain does not presently apply a continuous real-time digital stamping clearance model comparable to certain Latin American jurisdictions; instead, periodic or near-real-time filing through AEAT digital channels is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of LiFePO4 battery packs to third countries are VAT-exempt with the right to deduct input VAT under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law, applying an effective zero rate, provided the goods physically leave the EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter retains evidence of that departure. Intra-EU supplies are also exempt at 0% where the buyer is a taxable person with a valid EU VAT identification number and the goods are transported to another Member State, with the supply reported in the recapitulative statement. Services ancillary to the exported battery goods, such as freight and logistics, are eligible for zero-rating if contractually linked and evidenced. For offshore services, the place-of-supply generally follows the customer’s business establishment; where located outside the EU, the service is outside the Spanish VAT scope and no VAT is charged, but proof of customer status and actual use is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Documento Único Administrativo or DUA) duly validated by Spanish Customs
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or other transport document evidencing physical departure of the goods from EU customs territory
Commercial invoice, packing list, and purchase order
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Evidence of payment via SWIFT or telegraphic transfer corresponding to the export transaction
Intrastat and recapitulative statement or VIES records for intra-EU supplies where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Spanish Tax Administration applies strict audit scrutiny to export zero-rating claims, requiring documentary evidence of both the physical movement of goods and the commercial reality of the transaction. Claims for invoice-level VAT exemptions, export refunds, or 0% treatment may be retrospectively clawed back where documentation is missing, inconsistent, or fraudulent. Administrative penalties under the General Tax Law include a 50% to 150% penalty on the under-declared VAT amount, plus late-payment interest, and the denial of input VAT deductions. Where the false export documentation is linked to tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 in any single tax period, criminal tax fraud liability may arise under the Spanish Criminal Code, with penalties including imprisonment from one to six years and possible disqualification. The exporter bears the burden of proof; failure to repatriate or justify proceeds within the prescribed commercial payment term may be treated as a red flag for fictitious exports and trigger enhanced documentation requests.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) - central monetary authority, supervisor of credit and payment institutions, and custodian of the balance-of-payments statistical reporting regime under Real Decreto 472/2014; foreign direct investment declaration administration is vested in the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN), Secretaría de Estado de Comercio, Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo, with e-filing via the TELOS platform (Ley 19/2003).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility. As a euro-area member, the euro is fully transferable and payments for trade, services, dividends, intercompany loans and capital movements are freely executed without prior administrative authorization under Ley 19/2003 and the EU free movement of capital (Article 63 TFEU). No exchange control license, no prior Banco de España approval, and no minimum financing or repatriation obligation apply to bona fide commercial transactions. Profit remittance (dividends) is unrestricted after statutory corporate and tax compliance; non-resident dividend withholding is 19% under the Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax Code, reduced to 0-10% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or applicable DTTs. The only constraints are: (i) ex-post statistical declaration through bank-reported payment-purpose codes; (ii) post-closing FDI declaration in TELOS for foreign direct investments equal to or above EUR 3,000,000 or originating from tax-haven jurisdictions; and (iii) prior authorization requirements under Real Decreto-ley 34/2020 for non-EU/EFTA investors in reserved strategic sectors (defence, dual-use, critical infrastructure, energy, media, transport), which in principle do not capture standard LiFePO4 battery pack assembly but may trigger if R&D, dual-use or cyber-sensitive technology is embedded.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Spain imposes no statutory surrender, forced conversion, repatriation timeline, domiciliation or mandatory sales-channel requirement for export proceeds. Export invoices may be settled in euros or any freely convertible currency; proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts and converted at the exporter's discretion. The only obligations are (i) identification of the payment purpose for Banco de España balance-of-payments statistics, filed electronically by the resident credit institution under Real Decreto 472/2014, and (ii) documentary and tax justification of export transactions for Corporate Income Tax and customs purposes. No prior declaration or approval is required for settlement of export receivables.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (cuenta de capital for statutory SL deposit) + Operational Account (EUR and foreign-currency)
Capital Escrow Account + Operational Account (EUR and foreign-currency)
Capital Escrow Account + Operational Account (EUR and foreign-currency)
Operational Account (EUR and foreign-currency) + Trade Finance Desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for treasury-side operations, Low for trade finance and structural banking. EEA-authorised electronic money institutions and payment institutions (PSD2 / Ley 16/2009) passported into Spain may provide operational holding, SEPA and SWIFT MT103 receipt/disbursement, FX conversion and virtual IBANs for collections from Latin American and EU distributors. They cannot, however, issue or confirm letters of credit, provide committed credit lines, act as depositary for the statutory SL capital certificate required by the notary (Art. 62 Ley de Sociedades de Capital), or hold restricted regulatory escrows. Non-EEA EMIs, including UK fintechs post-Brexit, have no EU passport and require Spanish authorisation or an agency arrangement; their use is not recommended for compliance-critical flows (capital injection, LC issuance, statutory reserves). A licensed tier-1 bank account remains mandatory as the primary treasury spine, with EMIs used only as secondary collection rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted under Law 10/2010 and Real Decreto 304/2014 via qualified electronic signature (QES / certificado digital) or online video identification (PVID) where the bank's AML infrastructure provides equivalent assurance. In commercial practice, Spanish tier-1 banks require at least one director and every UBO above 25% to appear physically at a branch or before a notary, or to appoint a Spanish legal representative (apoderado) with targeted banking powers; wholly remote opening is generally available only at digital-first banks and still requires a Spanish-issued digital ID or notarised/apostilled foreign ID with video verification. Non-resident directors may satisfy the in-person mandate through the appointed Spanish representative, provided corporate documents (notarised deed, NIF, articles of association, apostilled certificates, translation by sworn translator) are lodged and UBO identity is verified by video call.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: capital injection from a non-EU shareholder resident in a high-risk or LATAM jurisdiction with source-of-funds opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised incorporation deed (Escritura) with the bank's Art. 62 LSC capital-deposit certificate; subscribed capital ledger and matching SWIFT MT103 instruction; sworn declaration of origin of funds; six-month personal and corporate bank statements of the contributor; tax residence certificates; corporate register excerpt and full UBO chain (natural persons above 25%) with apostilled IDs; written narrative of the legitimate business rationale for the Spanish entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: mismatch between declared manufacturing activity (ISIC 2720 battery pack assembly) and expected revenue, physical premises or operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease contract for the production plant (nave industrial) with utility invoices; purchase invoices for assembly lines and test equipment; payroll records and Spanish Social Security registration; production photographs and inventory list; ISO 9001, CE, UN 38.3 and RoHS certificates; municipal industrial licence (licencia de actividad) and environmental authorisation; genuine customer purchase orders and sales forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: industry sector flagged for ESG, conflict minerals, battery waste or dual-use criticality.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Battery producer registration under Directive 2006/66/EC (Spanish Registro de Productores de Pilas); REACH/RoHS compliance files; UN 38.3 transport test summary; OECD-aligned supply-chain due diligence report on lithium, iron phosphate and graphite sourcing; end-user declaration; confirmation that the LiFePO4 assembly process does not fall under Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2021/821 (dual-use list); environmental insurance and waste-management contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: large inbound foreign-currency capital increase or shareholder loan, especially via third-party payer or mixed-purpose payment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes approving the capital increase or intercompany loan; subscribed capital ledger; shareholder loan agreement (AML/ATAD-compliant documentation); SWIFT message with the correct Banco de España payment-purpose code (inversión directa or préstamo); source-of-funds statements; certification that the payer is the contractual counterparty; TELOS FDI declaration acknowledgement; updated beneficial-ownership register (RLUBO).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: transactions routed through intermediate distributors or subsidiaries in high-FX-risk or grey-listed jurisdictions with unusual payment cycles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed export sales contracts and commercial invoices with INCOTERMS 2020; packing lists; bills of lading or airway bills; export customs declarations; ultimate-customer KYC files; group treasury policy explaining routing and transfer-pricing rationale; certification that no party is listed on EU, UN, OFAC or Interpol sanctions or embargo registers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Pre-incorporation statutory capital: each subscriber transfers EUR (or convertible currency) via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA SCT if EEA) to the SL's capital escrow account at a Spanish tier-1 bank; the payment must reference the subscriber's name and the company being formed, and the bank issues the Art. 62 LSC certificate to the notary. Post-incorporation equity increases and shareholder loans: SWIFT MT103 with the company's NIF, purpose code 'EQUI' (ISO 20022) or the Spanish statistical concept code for direct investment (inversión directa) / shareholder loan (préstamo), accompanied by notarised board/shareholder minutes. The receiving bank files the mandatory balance-of-payments statistical declaration to Banco de España. The company must file the foreign-investment declaration via TELOS within the statutory deadline if the direct investment reaches EUR 3,000,000 or originates from a tax-haven jurisdiction. Verification pack: deed and registration certificate, updated UBO register, source-of-funds evidence, and tax clearance where relevant.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Intra-EEA and EUR-denominated supplier payments: SEPA Credit Transfers routed through T2/TARGET2-TIPS with immediate finality and no FX. Non-EEA or non-EUR disbursements: SWIFT MT103 customer transfers with UETR tracking and ISO 20022 purpose codes (e.g., 'TRAC' for trade, 'ADVA' for advance payment), cleared through correspondent banking (USD via CHIPS/Fedwire; CNY via CIPS; EUR via TARGET2). Trade settlement instruments for the LFP supply chain: (a) confirmed irrevocable letters of credit (SWIFT MT700/MT710, UCP600) for raw materials such as lithium carbonate, LFP cathode powder, separators and electrolytes, with reimbursement via MT754/MT202; (b) standby letters of credit or advance-payment guarantees (MT760) for capital equipment imports (cell assembly lines); (c) sight or deferred LCs for finished battery pack sales to EU and LATAM distributors; (d) trade loans, factoring and supply-chain finance facilities secured on verified invoices and open-account flows. Each instruction must carry INCOTERMS references, commercial invoice numbers and a structured remittance reference to satisfy bank trade surveillance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward outrights (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/INR) under ISDA 2002 or standard Spanish bank master terms with documented underlying commercial exposure
FX swaps (EUR/USD) for tenor-matched liquidity and rollover of payables/receivables
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL) to hedge non-euro debt or project revenues without conversion of the balance sheet
OTC currency options (call/put on EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, USD/MXN) with premium settled in EUR, subject to ISDA/CSA collateral
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or limited-convertibility LATAM currencies (e.g., ARS, VES) strictly backed by documented invoicing exposure and with bank-approved underlying contracts
Listed FX futures and options on EUR/USD at EU venues (e.g., MEFF or Eurex) for exchange-traded transparency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Cuentas Anuales) – balance sheet, profit and loss, statement of changes in equity and notes; approval and certification of shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved by shareholders within 6 months after fiscal year end (by 30 June for calendar-year companies) and filed within 1 month from approval, with practical filing deadline of 31 July for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties: EUR 1,200–6,000 for non-filing, plus administrative closure of the corporate tax registration (cierre registral) preventing further filings; repeated failure may lead to administrative dissolution or strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) – Modelo 200 / Form 200
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the 6-month period after the tax year end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, from 1 July to 25 July inclusive
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge: 1% of the tax due for each month of delay up to 20%, default interest at the legal rate, and penalties of 50–150% for inaccurate or incomplete filings; no direct strike-off but tax lien and asset seizure possible

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) Declaration and confirmation – affirmation of the corporate ownership chain and shareholding report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) linked to the Central Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Titularidades Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually together with the annual accounts filing before 31 July; any UBO change must be filed within 8 calendar days of the modification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML non-compliance penalties up to EUR 60,000 per infringement (Ley 10/2010), plus inability to obtain public subsidies or contracts; no strike-off trigger directly, but continued non-compliance may be reflected as a filing irregularity

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for SL if at least two of three conditions are met at year-end: total assets > EUR 2,850,000; annual turnover > EUR 5,700,000; average workforce > 50 employees. In addition, shareholders holding at least 5% of share capital may request an independent audit at the annual general meeting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC) as approved by RD 1514/2007, harmonised with EU-adopted IFRS for consolidated financial statements; individual-entity accounts follow national GAAP while group consolidations may use IFRS-Europe.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SL must maintain an internal book of ultimate beneficial owners (UBO) and, on an annual cycle coinciding with the annual accounts filing, reconfirm the registered ownership and control percentages with the Mercantile Registry. Changes to UBO details occurring during the year must be reported within 8 calendar days; the annual confirmation must be signed by the sole director or a joint signatory and filed electronically.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Attendance at General Meetings (Libro de Asistencia a Juntas)
Register of Contracts with the Sole Shareholder (Libro de Contratos del Socio Único)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 – 2,200 per annum (EUR 400–2,000) for a Spanish registered agent and/or commercial office address including local legal representation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,700 – 6,800 (EUR 1,500–6,000) for a statutory audit of a small-to-mid-sized SL, depending on turnover, assets and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created entities in the first two years of profitable activity (subject to conditions). Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely (no time limit).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) via AEAT electronic filing system (Sede Electrónica)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the 6-month period after the fiscal year-end (e.g., for calendar year-end Dec 31, deadline is July 25 of the following year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period (start and end dates of the fiscal year)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the exact fiscal year period; for non-residents, use the period as per the permanent establishment or Spanish-source income.
Provide the NIF assigned by AEAT for the non-resident entity or permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable base (after adjustments and loss carryforwards)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxable base from Spanish-source income only, applying applicable double tax treaty provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate (standard 25% or reduced 15% for new entities)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the standard 25% unless a treaty or special regime provides a lower rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax payable (after credits and withholdings)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any withholding tax credits and prepayments; ensure treaty relief is claimed via Form 210 or 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 5% of the tax due for each month of delay up to 20% (if filed within 12 months); after 12 months, penalty is 20% plus late interest. Non-filing may result in additional surcharges and criminal liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from their home tax authority and submit it to the Spanish paying entity. The paying entity must file Form 210 (for non-resident income) or Form 200 (if applicable) with AEAT, attaching the TRC. For EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, a 0% rate applies if the parent holds at least 5% of the subsidiary's capital for at least 12 months and meets substance requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 19%; treaty rates typically 5-10% (e.g., US-Spain treaty 5% for industrial royalties). Interest: statutory 19%; treaty rates often 0-10% (e.g., EU Interest and Royalties Directive allows 0% for related parties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Entities with net revenue ≥ €45 million must prepare Master File and Local File. For smaller entities, documentation is required if related-party transactions exceed €250,000 (for services) or €1 million (for other transactions).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies Economic Substance principles under EU ATAC and domestic anti-abuse rules. For manufacturing entities like battery pack assembly, substance requires physical presence, qualified staff, and operational decision-making in Spain to benefit from tax incentives and avoid recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of taxable income, falsification of invoices, or use of shell entities to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 150% of the evaded tax, plus late interest. Criminal prosecution for amounts exceeding €120,000 per year may result in imprisonment (1-5 years).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for unpaid taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox entity with no real economic activity, staff, or premises, solely to obtain tax benefits or avoid reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and penalties up to 25% of the tax base. Under EU ATAD, exit taxation may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes and penalties if they fail to ensure substance. Travel bans may be issued in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML controls, accepting cash payments above €10,000, or facilitating money laundering through trade-based schemes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €150,000 for minor infractions, up to €1.5 million for serious infractions, and criminal liability for directors involved in laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment (1-6 years) and confiscation of assets. Travel bans and professional disqualification may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for battery pack components or IP royalties that deviate from arm's length, resulting in profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustment to arm's length price, plus penalties of 15% on the adjusted amount (or 25% if non-compliance with documentation).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they approved the mispricing. In egregious cases, criminal tax evasion charges may apply.
